Every year, HOA boards and property managers across Florida hear the same complaints from their residents: slow internet during peak hours, service outages with no explanation, technicians who've never been to the property before, hold times measured in hours, and rates that creep up without warning. The reason is structural. National providers like Comcast and Spectrum use shared coax infrastructure that was never designed for today's bandwidth demands. They outsource their service calls to third-party contractors who are evaluated on speed, not quality. And when your board calls corporate, you're one of hundreds of thousands of accounts - nobody knows your property, nobody owns the relationship, and nobody is accountable. Your community is paying for a service model built around shareholder returns, not resident satisfaction. THE BROADSTAR ADVANTAGE A Better Model. Built Around Your Community. subpages.text: Skip to content Skip to content Menu Close sales@broadstar.com GET BULK INTERNET Search for: Home Fiber Benefits Services Bulk Fiber Internet BroadStreamTV BroadStar Support Vacation Hold Request Form Community Channel Find Your Community Page About Us Contact ACCOUNT Search for: Menu sales@broadstar.com Search for: Home Fiber Benefits Services Bulk Fiber Internet BroadStreamTV BroadStar Support Vacation Hold Request Form Community Channel Find Your Community Page About Us Contact ACCOUNT GET BULK INTERNET Every Unit Gets Its Own Fiber Pair Most community fiber networks split a single strand among dozens of homes. BroadStar builds an Active Optical Network, or AON. A dedicated fiber pair runs from our equipment straight to the unit, and it serves that unit only. What dedicated actually means In a shared network design, one fiber leaves the equipment room and is split among as many as 32 homes. Everyone on that branch draws from the same pool of capacity. It works fine at 10 in the morning. It behaves differently at 8 on a Tuesday night. AON gives every unit its own fiber and its own port on an active switch. There is no split, no shared branch, and no pool to draw down. A resident streaming in 4K does not change what the unit next door gets. The complaints your board hears are usually an architecture problem Boards tend to blame customer service when speeds sag in the evening. Slow service during peak hours is almost always the network design, not the support team. No amount of troubleshooting fixes a branch that is oversubscribed by design. This matters most on a long agreement. A bulk contract runs a decade.
